status: Built and tested offline: QUBO, QAOA, noise, DD/ZNE/PEC, resource estimator + sweeps, MIQP (exact DP), stats, theory, data-loader safeguards (mocked)
Needs your machine: real Yahoo/FRED/ESG data, Stim re-run, PyTorch agent test, Gurobi MIQP test, dashboard screenshots
Honest claim: rigorous bounds plus an empirical test; no quantum advantage shown at n up to 16

steps.title: The big picture
steps.sub: How the whole code runs, end to end
bullets: Data comes in: prices, VIX, ESG scores.
Every month we estimate returns (mu) and risk (Sigma).
We turn 'choose the best weights' into a QUBO: a yes/no puzzle over bits.
QAOA (a quantum circuit) tries to find the lowest-energy bit pattern.
Noise is added, then error mitigation or logical qubits are applied.
Classical solvers (exact, SA, MIQP, CVaR, RL) solve the same problem; a walk-forward backtest compares all of them.
steps.cap: run_all.py calls each box in this order, one command per stage.
steps.take: Each box is one file in qpo/. Numbers in this deck: SYNTHETIC DATA.

steps.title: Step 1 - Data
bullets: Real mode: fetch_data.py freezes Yahoo prices and FRED series to csv; every later stage runs offline from that snapshot.
ESG: build_esg.py converts Sustainalytics risk scores (lower = better) into a percentile score where higher = better.
Safeguards: macro series are never back-filled, truncated FRED series are dropped, pseudo-ESG is refused.
Offline mode: a synthetic market with calm and stress regimes and forced 2008-like and 2020-like crises (figure).
This deck was built from: SYNTHETIC DATA (meta.json data_source = synthetic).
steps.cap: Figure is the synthetic market used for tests and demos.
steps.take: Real runs must report survivorship bias and static-ESG look-ahead.

steps.title: Step 2 - Estimate return and risk
bullets: Use the last 252 trading days only (no look-ahead).
Expected return mu = half the asset's own mean + half the universe mean (shrinkage).
Covariance Sigma is shrunk 20% toward its diagonal.
ESG hard filter: assets with ESG < 40 are removed first.
Greedy pick of 3-4 assets (best Sharpe, low correlation) to fit on qubits.
VIX z-score sets risk aversion lambda_t and the weight cap (50% calm, 33% stress).
steps.cap: lambda_t = 6 x (1 + 0.5 x VIX_z).  Stress: cap drops from 3/6 to 2/6.
steps.take: Time-varying constraints come from this one step.

steps.title: Step 3 - Build the QUBO
bullets: A QUBO is: minimise x^T Q x with every x a bit.
Each weight = level/6, level = b0 + 2*b1: two bits per asset per period.
3 assets x 2 bits x 2 periods = 12 qubits (4096 candidate answers).
Q mixes: -return, +risk, +transaction cost, +budget penalty, +cap penalty, -ESG tilt.
Tests: Q matches the direct objective, and its optimum equals the hard-budget MIQP optimum.
steps.cap: Heatmap of Q for the 2008-10-15 instance (synthetic market).
steps.take: Red/blue cells are the couplings the circuit must encode.

steps.title: Step 4 - QAOA (the quantum part)
bullets: Start in an equal superposition of all bitstrings.
Repeat p times: a cost phase then an RX mixer.
Two angles per layer are tuned by COBYLA.
Adaptive depth: add layers (up to 3) only while the improvement exceeds 1%.
Sample bitstrings, evaluate their true energy classically, keep the best.
steps.cap: Optimum energy -0.031, random mean 2.149, QAOA (p=1) mean 0.663.
steps.take: P(optimum) = 0.0009 vs uniform 0.00024: boosted, but the optimum stays unlikely.

steps.title: Step 5 - Noise (NISQ+ model)
bullets: Gate, idle and readout errors are turned into an independent bit-flip probability q per qubit on the output string.
On this instance q is 0.026 (raw), 0.025 (with DD) and 1.0e-06 (logical).
Phenomenological model, not hardware truth.
steps.take: Dynamical decoupling only trims idle error, so it helps a little.

steps.title: Step 6a - Zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE)
bullets: Run at 1x, 2x and 3x noise.
Fit a curve and read it at 0x.
Cost: more runs and variance inflated by 19x (Richardson weights 3, -3, 1).
steps.take: ZNE reduces the bias but not completely.

steps.title: Step 6b - Probabilistic error cancellation (PEC)
bullets: The channel is known, so we apply its inverse with signed random samples.
On this instance PEC gives 0.6629 (ideal 0.6629): unbiased.
Price: gamma = (1-2q)^(-n); shots grow as gamma^2.
steps.take: This is why logical qubits are needed at scale.

steps.title: Step 7 - Logical qubits with Stim
bullets: Stim simulates the rotated surface code memory experiment, PyMatching decodes (d = 3, 5, 7).
Fit: p_L/round = A (p/p_th)^((d+1)/2) with A = 0.044, p_th = 0.0099 (9 points).
Logical mode injects the fitted logical flip rate into the small QAOA simulation.
Stim covers memory only; QAOA's non-Clifford gates are not simulated at code level.
steps.cap: Data exist for p = 2e-3..6e-3 only; lower p is an extrapolation.
steps.take: Say this clearly in the report.

steps.title: Step 8 - Resource estimation
bullets: Count rotations -> T gates, choose distance d, add T-factory area; failure budget split three ways (logical, synthesis, magic states).
n=16, p=1e-3: 75,576 physical qubits (range 49,232 - 88,758).
n=120, p=1e-3: 539,604 (range 183,480 - 1,180,620); needs 2-level distillation.
All constants are swept (assumptions table, tornado plot). Runtime is T-supply bound.
steps.take: Better hardware (p=1e-4) cuts the qubit count several-fold.

steps.title: Step 9 - Error-mitigation ablation
bullets: Each mitigation is switched on separately and in combination (9 configurations).
Raw error 0.112; ZNE 0.055; PEC 0.038.
DD+ZNE 0.045; DD+PEC 0.038; logical (d=7) 0.007.
Sampling overhead: ZNE 57x, PEC 12x.
steps.take: Mitigation helps estimation; logical qubits help most.

steps.title: Step 10 - Classical baselines
bullets: exact_qubo: brute force = true QUBO optimum (ceiling for QUBO solvers). sa_qubo: simulated annealing.
miqp_sub: hard-budget discrete problem, Gurobi MIQP if installed, else an exact DP (same optimum, cross-tested).
CVaR stochastic programs in HiGHS (and Gurobi when installed); equal weight.
RL: NumPy evolution-strategy agent; PyTorch REINFORCE agent written but NOT run in this build.
steps.cap: CVaR minimises average loss in the worst 10% of scenarios.
steps.take: The exact optimum lets us measure how far QAOA is from perfect.

steps.title: Step 11 - Walk-forward backtest
bullets: Every rebalance: build the QUBO from past data only, solve, trade, pay costs, hold.
Methods: 11.
GFC_2008: best classical cvar_sub Sharpe 1.17; QAOA logical 1.16; equal weight 0.67.
COVID_2020: best classical cvar_full Sharpe 0.37; QAOA logical -0.01; equal weight -0.34.
QUBO solvers differ little: the problem is tiny and the exact optimum is the ceiling.
steps.cap: SYNTHETIC DATA. These numbers say nothing about real markets.
steps.take: Tests confirm there is no look-ahead.

steps.title: Step 12 - Statistical significance
bullets: Paired stationary bootstrap on the Sharpe difference; Wilcoxon on per-period returns; Holm correction.
Result: 0 of 28 (GFC) and 0 of 28 (COVID) differences are significant.
Example: qaoa_ideal vs cvar_sub in 2008: diff -0.13, 95% CI [-0.48, +0.32].
Wide intervals mean low power: not significant is not the same as equal.
steps.take: No claim of quantum outperformance is supported by this table.

steps.title: Step 13 - Scaling and theory bounds
bullets: P1 noisy success >= ideal x (1-q)^n.  P2 Hoeffding shots.  P3 PEC cost gamma^2 (n=100, q=0.03: 2.4e5).  P4 ZNE variance x19.  P5 random baseline 2^n.  P6 noise budget shrinks like 1/n.
Empirical exponents (cost ~ 2^(s n)): QAOA 0.86, SA 0.43, random 1.00, Grover 0.50.
Six sizes, n <= 16: trend evidence only.
steps.cap: Honest result: the bounds are rigorous; an advantage is not shown.
steps.take: Grover's sqrt(2^n) curve is a reference line only.

steps.title: Step 14 - Live dashboard
bullets: Streamlit app replays market data tick by tick (synthetic or the real snapshot, with a banner saying which).
Every N ticks it rebuilds the QUBO from data seen so far and re-solves with each chosen method.
Shows P&L lines, weight bars and a table of solver gaps.
